Greetings all.

A lot has happened since my last trade posts and while I still do not have much free time to come in here, I will describe a GBP/USD trade that I took earlier today and still letting it run.

First chart and in reverse order (the opposite of what I used tell you) is of the 1hr.

Blue line shows support and resistance and has been proved over time to be and price where moves happen. On the top of the chart is a yellow box which indicates 1hr supply and today we got well into this area which is what I prefer to see happen, it is better to see a deep punch into the old areas where moves originated, rather than see a weak touch.

My stop as shown is above a nice bearish candle which removed the last of the weak holders i.e intra day bullish scalpers. The trade did not setup until we got back into this supply area earlier today and since I took and commented on these charts, the move down is slow and expected given it was getting late in the day and now just starting the Asian session. In time I do expect to see my lower target hit. I choose an old decision point as a near term target. Although at the time of writing I have moved my target lower of most of the trades.

Next chart is the 4hr. Again the blue line is from the 1hr chart as support and resistance and it is still making sense here, but not as clean as could be. We need some amount of artistic license when it comes to trading levels/areas. Note the last 4hr candle, when this candle closed shortly after I took this chart grab, it closed as a weak bullish candle with no signs of pro money being active. The next 4hr candle closed as a strong bearish engulfing candle. Using the logical side of your brain, if price fails to make new highs and is at old supply and is previously untested supply, the price has only one way to go.....unless there are reason(s) on higher time frames to continue the push up. But look at how much effort went in to reaching the price on this 4hr chart and look at where it stopped. On the bottom of the chart you will see my comment on fresh ground, eventually these prices get hit.

Final chart is of the daily. The yellow box is what is at first a confused looking support and resistance area and a single line does not show it up properly. I did put a line on the top of the box to show the most interesting area for support and one we may hit in the future. Remember, for prices to rise they must first fall. Why?.....unless pro money can get you stopped out, trading in the wrong direction etc they will not have enough profit margin to start the move and make it pay. Even on this chart we see two strong bullish days and this too is into 1hr, 4hr and daily supply. Does it make sense to be buying here?....that is a question only you can answer and you should have little hesitation in answering it.

While nothing is written in stone with trading you need to exercise caution to preserve capital and not be fixated in one direction and let a loosing trade burn you, Set a stop in case some unforeseen event tears up a perfect setup.

I had a nice Brent crude trade today but didnt get time to draw up a chart. In time I will get you all a few more trades as they happen rather than after the fact trades as seen on the experts on youtube when price has already moved.
